Tiden works beside your agents, whichever ones you use. It reads your code and writes down what your product does, as requirements kept versioned beside the code. Before a session starts, your agent gets a working contract: what you asked for, as promises, each one proven by a test. The session can't close while a promise is open. The requirement changes with the code on every merge. When something breaks in production, the error points back to the release and the change behind it. Every release carries its evidence: what was asked, what changed, what passed, and what happened after.

# Intent verification for coding agents. Meet Tiden.

Your agents write the code. Tiden verifies it does what you actually asked for.

Nikita Fedorov

Nikita Fedorov

Oct 6, 2026•7 min read

Today we're launching Tiden. It's a new product from the team behind Qase, built for one job: checking that the code your agents write does what you asked for.

We've been running it on our own code for months, and with a small group of customers since the summer. [...] Most tools in this space speed up one step of a process built around people writing the code. Tiden starts from a different assumption: agents write the code now, so every step around the code has to work differently.

Requirements are the record of what was asked for. Each change an agent makes is checked against them before it merges. Releases are gated on test evidence instead of a sign-off meeting. When something breaks in production, it goes back into the requirements, so the next change is checked against what actually broke.

That covers the whole cycle, from intent to production, and it keeps up with the agents.

Tiden is live at tiden.ai. Connect GitHub, and it maps the rest.

Tiden is also on Product Hunt. If you try it, we'd like to hear what you think there.

results.title: Coding Agents Write the Code. Who Verifies It Works? We Built the Answer. - Qovery Blog
results.content:
But security demands isolation, and verification demands access to real infrastructure. Every vendor chose security. Verification stays unsolved.

The result is a gap. The agent writes the code in a sandbox. A human deploys it to a real environment and verifies it works. The loop stays broken.

### Cursor said it themselves

Cursor's engineering team published their findings from building and scaling cloud agents. Their conclusions:

Cursor ended up building what they describe as "essentially enterprise IT for agents" - secret redaction, network policies, credential management. They migrated to Temporal for durable execution handling 50 million actions per day across 7 million workflows. All of that infrastructure to give agents a real working environment. [...] The current generation of AI coding agents includes:

 GitHub Copilot coding agent - assign a GitHub issue and it works autonomously inside GitHub Actions.
 OpenAI Codex - runs tasks in parallel sandboxes, powered by the codex-1 model.
 Claude Code - triggered by an `@claude` mention in any PR or issue.
 Cursor cloud agents - background agents that handle tasks in isolated VMs.
 Gemini and OpenCode - additional runtimes gaining adoption.

These tools are genuinely effective at the generation step. Where every one of them stops short is the same place: verifying that the code actually works in a real environment. That gap - not code quality - is the real bottleneck, and it's what the rest of this article is about.

## The broken loop

Every developer knows the real loop: [...] Last week I assigned a Linear issue to a coding agent. Straightforward feature - add a filter to an API endpoint, update the tests, adjust the docs. Ten minutes later I had a PR. The code looked clean. The sandbox tests passed.

Qovery · Agentic Infrastructure Platform

Build with Claude Code, Deploy with Qovery

Learn more

Then the real work started. I pulled the branch, spun up my local environment, configured the database seed, launched the app, clicked through the feature manually, found two edge cases the agent missed where the filter broke on empty arrays, pushed fixes, waited for CI. The "10-minute PR" cost me an hour of verification.

The agent did the easy part.

## Coding agents work

Coding agents work. They're not a gimmick.
